presets.name: Gyroid
eq: sin x cos y + sin y cos z + sin z cos x = 0
presets.note: Found by Alan Schoen in 1970. It splits space into two identical intertwined labyrinths and contains no straight lines.
presets.clip: mix(length(p) - 1.22, length(max(abs(p) - 0.66, 0.0)) + min(max(abs(p.x) - 0.66, max(abs(p.y) - 0.66, abs(p.z) - 0.66)), 0.0) - 0.14, box)

presets.name: Gyroid lattice
eq: sin x cos y + sin y cos z + sin z cos x > c
presets.note: One of the gyroid’s two labyrinths, filled in.

presets.name: Tanglecube
presets.note: Eight blobs at the corners of a cube. Lower c and they reach out and join.
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ vec3 a = q*q; return dot(a, a) - 5.0*(a.x + a.y + a.z) + tangle; }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 2.5500); }

presets.name: Chmutov quartic
presets.note: Built from Chebyshev polynomials, the ones that wiggle evenly between −1 and 1. Take c below zero and it breaks into pebbles.
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ vec3 a = q*q; vec3 t = 8.0*a*a - 8.0*a + 1.0; return t.x + t.y + t.z - cheb; }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 1.3300); }

presets.name: Chmutov sextic
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ vec3 a = q*q; vec3 t = 32.0*a*a*a - 48.0*a*a + 18.0*a - 1.0; return t.x + t.y + t.z - cheb; }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 1.3600); }

presets.name: Decocube
presets.note: A ring on every face of a cube, fused where they meet.
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ vec3 a = q*q; float c2 = 0.64; return ((a.x + a.y - c2)*(a.x + a.y - c2) + (a.z - 1.0)*(a.z - 1.0)) * ((a.y + a.z - c2)*(a.y + a.z - c2) + (a.x - 1.0)*(a.x - 1.0)) * ((a.z + a.x - c2)*(a.z + a.x - c2) + (a.y - 1.0)*(a.y - 1.0)) - deco; }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 1.2000); }

presets.name: Orthocircles
presets.note: Three circles at right angles, thickened until they merge.
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ vec3 a = q*q; float r2 = a.x + a.y + a.z; return ((a.x + a.y - 1.0)*(a.x + a.y - 1.0) + a.z) * ((a.y + a.z - 1.0)*(a.y + a.z - 1.0) + a.x) * ((a.z + a.x - 1.0)*(a.z + a.x - 1.0) + a.y) - ortho*ortho*(1.0 + 3.0*r2); }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 1.0000); }

presets.name: Double torus
presets.note: A surface with two holes: a doughnut for two.
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ float w = q.x*q.x*(1.0 - q.x*q.x) - q.y*q.y; return w*w + q.z*q.z - holes; }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 0.9000); }

presets.name: Heart
presets.note: Taubin’s heart surface: a sixth-degree polynomial.
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ vec3 h = q.xzy; float a = h.x*h.x + 2.25*h.y*h.y + h.z*h.z - 1.0; return a - h.z * pow(h.x*h.x + 0.1125*h.y*h.y + 1e-9, 1.0/3.0); }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 1.0200); }

presets.name: Kummer surface
eq: p, q, r, s: the four faces of a tetrahedron
presets.note: A quartic with sixteen cone points, the most a quartic can have.
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ float m2 = mu; float lam = (3.0*m2 - 1.0) / (3.0 - m2); const float R2 = 1.41421356; float p1 = 1.0 - q.z - R2*q.x, p2 = 1.0 - q.z + R2*q.x, p3 = 1.0 + q.z + R2*q.y, p4 = 1.0 + q.z - R2*q.y; float a = dot(q, q) - m2; return a*a - lam*p1*p2*p3*p4; }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 2.3000); }

presets.name: Barth sextic
presets.note: Sixty-five cone points, the most a sixth-degree surface can have, arranged with the symmetry of an icosahedron. φ is the golden ratio.
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ const float ph = 1.618034; vec3 a = q*q; return side * (4.0*(ph*ph*a.x - a.y)*(ph*ph*a.y - a.z)*(ph*ph*a.z - a.x) - (1.0 + 2.0*ph)*(a.x + a.y + a.z - 1.0)*(a.x + a.y + a.z - 1.0)); }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 1.9000); }

presets.name: Clebsch cubic
eq: 81(x³ + y³ + z³) − 189(x²y + x²z + y²x + y²z + z²x + z²y)
+ 54xyz + 126(xy + yz + zx) − 9(x² + y² + z²) − 9(x + y + z) + 1 = 0
presets.note: A cubic surface containing 27 straight lines, all of them real.
presets.glsl:
float f(vec3 q){ float x = q.x, y = q.y, z = q.z; return 81.0*(x*x*x + y*y*y + z*z*z) - 189.0*(x*x*y + x*x*z + y*y*x + y*y*z + z*z*x + z*z*y) + 54.0*x*y*z + 126.0*(x*y + y*z + z*x) - 9.0*(x*x + y*y + z*z) - 9.0*(x + y + z) + 1.0; }
float raw(vec3 p){ return f(p * 1.1000); }
